summary: A 1941 ground cabin on Deadman Mountain in Lincoln County, Wyoming, registered in 2022 and described as severely deteriorated but still standing.

facts.design: Ground cabin in the unusual four-window-panel design, identical to the Cabin Creek Peak cabin
facts.status_note: Register (2022) calls it severely deteriorated but still standing; a Komoot hiking listing says it has since been abandoned.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Bridger National Forest

events.note: Register and firelookout.com give 1941. A July 1941 newspaper item describes a carpentry crew building a fire lookout there. An August 1940 item mentions a fire lookout site while a telephone line was built to it; the sources do not settle whether an earlier structure stood there.

evidence.supports: constructed 1941; severely deteriorated but still standing
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1941, the structure is severely deteriorated but still standing.

evidence.supports: unusual four-window-panel design, identical to Cabin Creek Peak
evidence.quote: The ground cabin at Deadman Mountain is another of the unusual 4 window panel lookout designs. The cabin is identical to Cabin Creek Peak.

evidence.supports: administered by US Forest Service, Bridger National Forest
evidence.quote: US Forest Service - Bridger National Forest

evidence.supports: Greyfall alternate name; Lincoln County; Bridger National Forest

evidence.quote: Lincoln County - Bridger National Forest - T35N-R116W-22

evidence.supports: carpentry crew building a fire lookout on Dead Man Mountain
evidence.quote: The carpentry crew under foreman Mike Buol is building a fire lookout on Dead Man Mountain on Gray's river.

evidence.supports: 1940 telephone line to Dead Man mountain point, fire lookout
evidence.quote: emergency telephone line from Alpine to Dead Man mountain point, fire lookout

evidence.supports: August 1940 item: foreman assigned to oversee construction of the telephone line
evidence.quote: has been assigned to oversee the construction of an emergency telephone line from Alpine

evidence.supports: built in the 1940s on the summit; since abandoned; views from inside on a clear day
evidence.quote: Deadman Lookout was built in the 1940's on the summit of Deadman Mountain. It has since been abandoned but from inside on a clear day a visitor can enjoy views of the Wyoming Range, Salt River Range, and even the Tetons.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and West Lookouts name Bridger National Forest; firelookout.com names Bridger-Teton National Forest. The record keeps the register's agency name and the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The 1941 build year is supported by the register, firelookout.com and a 1941 newspaper item reprinted on West Lookouts, which is a secondary transcription. The 1940 telephone-line item calls the site a fire lookout before the 1941 build report; I could not settle whether an earlier structure stood there. The abandonment claim comes from a hiking listing, not an agency record. No staffing, fire or current access source was found, so none is stated. Brief record checked: the name, elevation, agency and 2022 registration match, so no corrections were needed. Not reached: Bridger-Teton or Bridger NF lookout records, and the NHLR nomination file for WY 21.
